Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork as discrete documents with typed fields (identifier, date, status), routes each item through a single named channel, and preserves each intake in its original form for later audit review.

2) What occurred: The actor recorded a single valid ticket document into a ticket registry, noting its identifier, the dated record of its status, and the named account holding it. The actor then duplicated the document, generating several additional copies, each with an identifier field and a status field reflecting the original. The actor set a field indicating the named account was to hold the record, then moved the original document through the ticket exchange channel to a buyer account. Finally, the actor marked the refund and chargeback fields on the original document as closed, and marked the identification field on the buyer record as void.

3) Materials/access observed: A single ticket document with an identifier, a dated record, and a named account field. Several duplicate copies of the same document, each with matching identifier and status fields. A ticket exchange channel for document transfer. A refund field, a chargeback field, and an identification field, each with a status value.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Multiple document copies with identical identifier fields but distinct record entries in the ticket registry. A transfer entry in the exchange channel showing a single document moving to a buyer account. Refund and chargeback fields on the original document marked closed. An identification field on the buyer record marked void.
